findings.title: TestLogger.FromContext returns a fresh logger, so logged calls are lost
findings.body: `TestLogger.FromContext` returns `NewTestLogger()` instead of `f`. `LoggerMiddleware` now logs only through `m.logger.FromContext(ctx).Info(...)`, so every log call goes to a throwaway instance. The `InfoLogs`/`ErrorLogs` counters on the TestLogger handed to the middleware never change. Any test asserting on what the middleware logged will silently see zero calls. `New` has the same problem. Return `f` so calls are recorded on the logger the test holds.

findings.title: ContextualLoggerMiddleware dereferences req without a nil check
findings.body: `QueryData`, `CallResource`, `CheckHealth` and `CollectMetrics` read `req.PluginContext` unconditionally. A nil request therefore panics here. `LoggerMiddleware`, the next middleware, explicitly guards against `req == nil` and passes the call through. The two adjacent middlewares are inconsistent, and the new one panics where the old logging path tolerated nil. Add the same nil guard, or document that requests are never nil.

findings.title: Request log fields now depend implicitly on ContextualLoggerMiddleware ordering
findings.body: `pluginId`, `endpoint`, `uname`, `dsName`, `dsUID` and `traceID` used to be added explicitly in `logRequest`. They are now expected to come from the context via `FromContext`. That only works if `ContextualLoggerMiddleware` runs earlier in the chain and the infra logger's context provider supplies `traceID`. If `LoggerMiddleware` is used on its own, or the middlewares are reordered, the 'Plugin Request Completed' log line silently loses these identifying fields. Dashboards and alerts built on the grafana-data-egress event depend on them. Document the ordering requirement or keep the essential fields explicit.

findings.title: Adding FromContext to the Logger interface breaks other implementations
findings.body: Adding a method to the exported `plog.Logger` interface is a breaking change. Any other implementation inside or outside this package (fakes, wrappers, enterprise code) will no longer compile until it implements `FromContext`. The doc comment is also inaccurate: it says the returned logger has "this logger's context plus the given context", but it actually adds the contextual attributes stored in the `context.Context`.
